#!/bin/bash
#flux: --ntasks=4
#flux: --gpus-per-node=1
#flux: --mem-per-node=4G
#flux: --output=logs/job_%J.out
#flux: --error=logs/job_%J.err
# The Slurm partition directive '-p mhigh,mhigh' has no direct Flux equivalent.
# This is typically handled by resource constraints on the target system. You may
# need to add a '--constraint' option if the system uses node features to define partitions.
# The Slurm memory directive '--mem 4096' was translated to '--mem-per-node=4G'.
# This assumes the 4 tasks will be placed on a single node, which is common for small jobs.
# The Slurm output/error format '%x_%u_%j' (jobname_user_jobid) was partially translated.
# Flux supports '%J' for job ID but not equivalents for job name or user. The filenames have
# been set to 'logs/job_%J.out' and 'logs/job_%J.err'.

python task_b.py \
    --loss "contrastive" \
    --miner "PairMargin" \
	--output_path "outputs_task_b/" \
    --dataset "mit_split" \
    --dataset_config_path "./configs/mit_split.yaml" \
    --dataset_path "/home/mcv/datasets/MIT_split/" \
	--model resnet_18 \
    --embedding_size 256 \
	--batch_size 64 \
    --epochs 20

issues: The job requests 4 tasks ('--ntasks=4') but only launches a single serial Python script. This means 3 of the 4 allocated CPU cores will remain idle, leading to inefficient use of allocated resources. If the Python script is multi-threaded, a more appropriate request would be '--ntasks=1 --cpus-per-task=4'.

Machine learning tasks of this nature typically require a GPU to run. Without a GPU, the application will either fail immediately if it depends on CUDA, or it will run on the CPU at a speed that is orders of magnitude slower, likely making it impossible to complete within a reasonable timeframe.
